rules.title: Equipment bonus rules
rules.calculationText: Item bonuses are not added directly together. A full setup uses a weighted calculation so equipment gives a realistic support advantage without replacing rider skill.
rules.balanceText: Even if every selected item has a strong bonus, the equipment setup bonus is capped. This prevents a weak rider with perfect equipment from becoming better than a much stronger rider.
rules.example: Example: if all six equipment items have Flat +4%, the setup does not become +24%. It is weighted by category and capped around +4%. Specialist equipment can include trade-offs, shown in red. For example, a pure climbing item may give Mountain +4% but Flat -1% and Sprint -2%.

tutorial.welcomeBody: We can show you how Equipment works, including race setups, inventory, market purchases, and race supplies.
tutorial.overviewBody:
This is the Equipment page.

The Overview tab gives you a summary of your team equipment and your race setup configurations.

The Default Race Setup is the setup used when you do not choose a specific setup for a race. Below that, you can create different race setup configurations that can later be selected in Race Preparation.

Each setup can bring different bonuses to your riders, depending on the equipment inside it and how many usable items are available.
tutorial.inventoryBody:
The Inventory tab shows all equipment your team currently owns.

Here you can see items such as bikes, wheels, tires, and other equipment you purchased. You can check quality, condition, value, bonuses, and availability.

If you no longer need some equipment, you can sell it from your inventory.
tutorial.marketBody:
The Market tab is where you buy new equipment.

Each item has a price and can bring different bonuses. Better equipment can improve race performance, but it also costs more.

When you purchase equipment, it is sent to your Inventory and can later be used in race setups.
tutorial.suppliesBody:
The Race Supplies tab shows consumable supplies your team can use for races.

Some supplies can be used only once, while others may be used multiple times. Supplies can help protect riders from difficult race conditions.

Without the right race supplies, riders may receive negative effects in very hot, cold, or demanding weather conditions.

After Equipment, the next recommended page is Infrastructure.
